question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. Litmus is a natural indicator obtained from lichens.
II. Turmeric turns red when it comes into contact with an acidic solution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is CORRECT. Litmus is a natural indicator extracted from lichens — a composite organism formed by algae and fungi living together. (लिटमस — लाइकेन से प्राप्त)

 

• In its neutral state litmus is purple. It turns red in acid and blue in base.

 

• Statement II is INCORRECT. Turmeric turns RED in a BASIC solution, not in an acidic one. In acid it remains yellow, its natural colour.

 

• This is why a spot of turmeric on a white shirt turns red when soap — which is basic — is rubbed on it, and goes back to yellow when the soap is washed away.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Natural indicators: litmus (from lichens), turmeric, red cabbage juice, china rose (hibiscus) petals — which turn magenta in acid and green in base.

 

• Synthetic indicators: methyl orange (red in acid, yellow in base) and phenolphthalein (colourless in acid, pink in base).

 

• Olfactory indicators are substances whose smell changes with the medium — onion and vanilla essence lose their smell in a base.

 

NOTE

 

• Since Statement I is correct and Statement II is not, Option 2 (Only II), Option 3 (Both I and II) and Option 4 (Neither I nor II) are all ruled out.

 

• The trap in Statement II is a true colour attached to the wrong medium. In statement questions of this kind, check the medium as carefully as the colour.

question: Coal India Limited, the largest coal producing company in the world, was formed in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1975.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Coal India Limited (CIL) was formed in November 1975, with its headquarters at Kolkata. (कोल इंडिया लिमिटेड — 1975)

 

• It is the largest coal producing company in the world, and accounts for the great majority of India's coal output.

 

• It was created by bringing together the nationalised coal companies under a single holding company, and it operates today through subsidiaries such as Eastern Coalfields, Bharat Coking Coal, Central Coalfields, South Eastern Coalfields, Northern Coalfields, Western Coalfields and Mahanadi Coalfields.

 

• It was granted Maharatna status in 2011.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The nationalisation of coal proceeded in stages:

 

• 1971 – the coking coal mines were taken over

 

• 1972 – Bharat Coking Coal Limited was formed

 

• 1973 – the non-coking coal mines were taken over, and Coal Mines Authority Limited was set up

 

• 1975 – Coal India Limited was formed as the holding company

 

• India is the second largest producer and consumer of coal in the world, after China. The largest producing states are Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.

 

NOTE

 

• 1971 (Option 1): The year the coking coal mines were nationalised, under the Coking Coal Mines (Emergency Provisions) Act.

 

• 1973 (Option 2): The year the non-coking coal mines were nationalised and the Coal Mines Authority Limited was set up — the immediate predecessor of Coal India, and the strongest distractor here.

 

• 1980 (Option 4): The year in which the second round of bank nationalisation took place, and no landmark in the coal industry.

question: Which is the longest lake in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vembanad Lake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vembanad Lake, in Kerala, is the longest lake in India — about 96 km in length — and the longest in India by any measure of extent along its axis. (वेम्बनाड झील — भारत की सबसे लंबी झील)

 

• It is a backwater lagoon, separated from the Arabian Sea by a narrow strip of land, and it spreads across the districts of Alappuzha, Kottayam and Ernakulam.

 

• It is a Ramsar site, designated in 2002, and the largest wetland in Kerala.

 

• The Nehru Trophy Boat Race, the great snake-boat race held every August at Punnamada, takes place on this lake.

 

• The Thanneermukkom bund was built across it to keep salt water out of the Kuttanad paddy fields, which lie below sea level — the only such farming in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lakes worth distinguishing:

 

• Longest – Vembanad (Kerala)

 

• Largest freshwater – Wular (Jammu & Kashmir)

 

• Largest saltwater / largest brackish lagoon – Chilika (Odisha)

 

• Largest inland salt lake – Sambhar (Rajasthan)

 

• Highest – Cholamu (Sikkim)

 

• Largest artificial – Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar / Rihand (Uttar Pradesh)

 

NOTE

 

• Chilika Lake (Option 2): In Odisha, the largest brackish water lagoon in India and the second largest in the world. It is famous for its migratory birds and for the Irrawaddy dolphin. It is larger in area than Vembanad, which makes it the strongest distractor — but the question asks which is longest.

 

• Wular Lake (Option 3): In Jammu & Kashmir, the largest freshwater lake in India, fed by the Jhelum.

 

• Kolleru Lake (Option 4): In Andhra Pradesh, between the deltas of the Godavari and the Krishna, and a Ramsar site.

question: A crescent-shaped lake formed when a meander is cut off from the main channel of a river is called _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is an oxbow lake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An OXBOW LAKE is a crescent-shaped lake formed when a meander — a large loop in a river's course — is cut off from the main channel. (गोखुर झील / चापाकार झील)

 

• The process is a steady one and is worth following:

 

• A river flowing over a plain erodes the outer bank of a bend, where the current is swiftest, and deposits material on the inner bank, where it is slowest.

 

• The loop grows narrower at its neck.

 

• In time of flood the river cuts across the neck, taking the shorter course.

 

• The abandoned loop is sealed off by deposition and remains as a crescent-shaped lake.

 

• The name comes from its shape, which resembles the U-shaped collar (bow) placed on the neck of an ox.

 

• Oxbow lakes are common on the plains of the Ganga and the Brahmaputra, where the rivers meander freely.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fluvial landforms and where they occur:

 

• Upper course (erosion) – V-shaped valleys, gorges, waterfalls, potholes

 

• Middle course (transport) – meanders, oxbow lakes, alluvial fans, floodplains

 

• Lower course (deposition) – levees, deltas, estuaries, distributaries

 

NOTE

 

• a lagoon (Option 1): A shallow body of water separated from the sea by a sandbar or a coral reef. It is a coastal feature, formed by the sea rather than by a river — Chilika and Pulicat are examples.

 

• a delta (Option 3): The triangular deposit of silt formed where a river enters the sea and its distributaries spread out. The Sundarbans delta is the largest in the world.

 

• an estuary (Option 4): The funnel-shaped mouth of a river where it meets the sea and fresh and salt water mix. Rivers such as the Narmada and the Tapi form estuaries rather than deltas, because they flow through rift valleys and carry little silt.

question: Which plant tissue gives flexible mechanical support to young stems and leaf stalks, and is found just beneath the epidermis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Collenchyma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• COLLENCHYMA provides mechanical support together with flexibility to the young growing parts of a plant, and lies just beneath the epidermis of stems and leaf stalks. (कोलेन्काइमा)

 

• Its cells are living, elongated, and thickened at the corners by deposits of cellulose and pectin. The thickening gives strength; the fact that the cells remain living gives the tissue its power to stretch.

 

• This is why the stems of climbers can bend in the wind without breaking — a rigid tissue would snap.

 

• Collenchyma is one of the three simple permanent tissues of plants, along with parenchyma and sclerenchyma.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three simple permanent tissues compared:

 

• PARENCHYMA – thin-walled living cells; the basic packing tissue; stores food and water. When it contains chlorophyll it is called chlorenchyma and performs photosynthesis; when it has large air cavities it is aerenchyma, which keeps aquatic plants afloat.

 

• COLLENCHYMA – living, thickened at the corners; flexible support.

 

• SCLERENCHYMA – dead cells with walls thickened by lignin; gives rigid strength and hardness. It forms the husk of the coconut and the fibres of jute.

 

NOTE

 

• Parenchyma (Option 1): The basic packing tissue, thin-walled and unspecialised. It stores food but gives little mechanical support.

 

• Aerenchyma (Option 2): A form of parenchyma with large air spaces, found in aquatic plants such as the water hyacinth, which it keeps buoyant.

 

• Sclerenchyma (Option 3): Gives strength, but its cells are dead and lignified, so the support it gives is rigid, not flexible. This is the distinction the question turns on.

question: Who was the founder of the Gupta dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sri Gupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The founder of the Gupta dynasty was SRI GUPTA, who ruled in about 240-280 CE. (गुप्त वंश के संस्थापक — श्रीगुप्त)

 

• He and his son Ghatotkacha bore only the modest title "Maharaja", which suggests they were feudatory rulers rather than independent sovereigns.

 

• The point on which this question turns is the difference between the founder of the dynasty and the founder of the empire:

 

• Sri Gupta – founded the dynasty

 

• Chandragupta I – founded the empire. He was the first to take the title "Maharajadhiraja", married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi, and is believed to have begun the Gupta era in 319-320 CE.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gupta rulers in order: Sri Gupta → Ghatotkacha → Chandragupta I → Samudragupta → Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) → Kumaragupta I → Skandagupta.

 

• Samudragupta is known from the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti), composed by his court poet Harishena, and is called the "Napoleon of India" by V.A. Smith.

 

• Chandragupta II defeated the Shakas, and the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign. The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli is associated with a king named Chandra.

 

• The Gupta age is called the "Golden Age of India" for its achievements in literature, mathematics, astronomy and sculpture — Kalidasa, Aryabhata and Varahamihira all belong to it.

 

NOTE

 

• Chandragupta I (Option 2): The answer most candidates give, and the founder of the empire — but the third ruler of the line, not its founder.

 

• Samudragupta (Option 3): The greatest of the Gupta conquerors, and the son of Chandragupta I.

 

• Ghatotkacha (Option 4): The son of Sri Gupta and the second ruler of the dynasty. Note that he is not the Ghatotkacha of the Mahabharata.

question: "Siddi Dhamal", performed by a community of African descent settled in India, is a folk dance of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Siddi Dhamal, also called Dhamaal, is performed by the Siddi community of GUJARAT, settled chiefly in the Junagadh and Gir Somnath districts. (सिद्दी धमाल — गुजरात)

 

• The Siddis are descended from Africans — mainly from the Bantu peoples of south-east Africa — who came to India from about the twelfth century onwards as traders, sailors, soldiers and slaves.

 

• The dance retains a distinctly African character: it is driven by drumming on the Mugarman (a large drum), the Mai Misra and the Malunga (a musical bow), and the dancers move in a fast circle, using coconut shells and peacock feathers.

 

• It is performed at weddings, at festivals and at the shrine of the Siddi saint Bava Gor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Siddi communities are also found in Karnataka (Uttara Kannada), Maharashtra and Hyderabad, and are recognised as a Scheduled Tribe in Gujarat, Karnataka and elsewhere.

 

• Other folk dances of Gujarat: Garba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani (performed by women of the Chorwad region while beating the floor), Padhar, Hudo and Bhavai.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Has a Siddi population descended from the rulers of Janjira, but the Dhamal dance is associated with Gujarat. Maharashtra's own folk forms are Lavani, Tamasha, Powada and Gondhal.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Also has a substantial Siddi community in Uttara Kannada, which makes it a genuine distractor. Its own folk dances are Dollu Kunitha, Veeragase and Yakshagana.

 

• Goa (Option 4): Known for Dekhni, Fugdi, Ghode Modni and Mando — none of them connected with the Siddis.

question: "Kummi", performed by women standing in a circle and clapping in rhythm, is a folk dance of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kummi is one of the oldest folk dances of TAMIL NADU, performed by women standing in a circle and clapping their hands in rhythm as they move. (कुम्मी — तमिलनाडु)

 

• It requires no musical instrument at all — the clapping of the hands supplies the whole of the rhythm, and the dancers sing as they go. It is said to date from a time before instruments were in common use.

 

• It is danced at Pongal, at temple festivals and at family celebrations, and has many local forms — Poo Kummi (with flowers), Deepa Kummi (with lamps) and Kulavai Kummi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Tamil Nadu: Kolattam (danced with sticks, and the natural companion of Kummi), Karagattam (balancing a decorated pot on the head), Kavadi Attam, Oyilattam, Mayilattam (the peacock dance) and Therukoothu (street theatre).

 

• The classical dance of Tamil Nadu is Bharatanatyam, among the eight classical dances of India, and the state's great temple festival is Pongal, celebrated in January.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Known for Thiruvathirakali — also a circular women's dance, which makes this the closest distractor — and for Kaikottikali, Theyyam, Padayani and the classical Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): Known for Dollu Kunitha, Veeragase, Kamsale and Yakshagana.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Known for Kuchipudi (classical), and for Veeranatyam, Butta Bommalu and Dhimsa.

question: The "International Kite Festival", held every year on Uttarayan, is celebrated chiefly in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Kite Festival is held every year at AHMEDABAD, Gujarat, on the banks of the Sabarmati. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय पतंग महोत्सव — अहमदाबाद)

 

• It is held on 14 January, the day of Uttarayan — the festival marking the sun's northward journey, known elsewhere in India as Makar Sankranti.

 

• It has been organised by the Gujarat government since 1989, and draws kite-flyers from dozens of countries.

 

• Ahmedabad also has a Kite Museum, the only one of its kind in India, at the Sanskar Kendra designed by Le Corbusier.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same day, under different names across India:

 

• Uttarayan – Gujarat; Makar Sankranti – much of northern and western India

 

• Pongal – Tamil Nadu; Magh Bihu / Bhogali Bihu – Assam

 

• Lohri – Punjab, on the preceding evening

 

• Poush Parbon – West Bengal; Khichdi – Uttar Pradesh and Bihar

 

• It is one of the few Indian festivals fixed to the solar calendar, which is why it falls on almost the same date every year.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaipur (Option 2): Also has a well-known kite festival on Makar Sankranti, which makes it the strongest distractor — but the International festival, and the older and larger of the two, belongs to Ahmedabad. Jaipur is better known for the Jaipur Literature Festival and the Elephant Festival.

 

• Lucknow (Option 3): Known for the Lucknow Mahotsav and for its association with kathak and chikankari.

 

• Bhopal (Option 4): Known for the Bharat Bhavan and the Lokrang festival held in January.

question: The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC), where India's launch vehicles are designed and developed, is located at _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thiruvananthapuram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) is at THIRUVANANTHAPURAM, Kerala, and is ISRO's lead centre for the design and development of launch vehicles. (विक्रम साराभाई अंतरिक्ष केंद्र — तिरुवनंतपुरम)

 

• The SLV, ASLV, PSLV and GSLV were all developed here.

 

• It grew out of the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS), from which India's first sounding rocket was launched on 21 November 1963. Thumba was chosen because it lies almost exactly on the magnetic equator.

 

• It was renamed in 1972 after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the father of the Indian space programme, who died in 1971.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The principal centres of ISRO and what each does:

 

• VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram – launch vehicles

 

• U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), Bengaluru – satellites

 

• Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), Sriharikota – launching

 

• Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad – payloads and applications

 

• ISRO Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network (ISTRAC), Bengaluru – tracking

 

• Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC), Valiamala and Mahendragiri – liquid engines

 

• ISRO's headquarters is at Bengaluru, and it was founded on 15 August 1969.

 

NOTE

 

• Sriharikota (Option 1): In Andhra Pradesh, the site of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre — India's launch site, not the place where the vehicles are built. This is the strongest distractor.

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 3): Site of the Space Applications Centre, and also of the Physical Research Laboratory founded by Sarabhai himself in 1947.

 

• Hyderabad (Option 4): Site of the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), which receives and processes satellite data.

question: Which planet of the solar system rotates from east to west, so that on it the sun appears to rise in the west?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Venus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• VENUS rotates on its axis from east to west — the reverse of the earth and of almost every other planet. On Venus, therefore, the sun rises in the west and sets in the east. (शुक्र — पूर्व से पश्चिम घूर्णन)

 

• This is called retrograde rotation, and it is believed to have been caused by a massive collision early in the planet's history.

 

• Venus turns extraordinarily slowly. A single rotation takes about 243 earth days, while its revolution round the sun takes about 225 days — so a day on Venus is longer than its year.

 

• Venus is also the hottest planet in the solar system, with a surface temperature of about 465°C, because its dense atmosphere of carbon dioxide traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect. It is hotter than Mercury, though further from the sun.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Venus is called the "Morning Star" and the "Evening Star", being the brightest object in the sky after the sun and the moon. It is also called the "Earth's twin" for its similar size and mass — though in every other respect the two could hardly be less alike.

 

• Uranus also rotates in a retrograde sense, but its axis is tilted by about 98 degrees, so that it effectively rolls on its side as it goes round the sun.

 

• India's mission to Venus is the Shukrayaan orbiter, approved for launch later this decade.

 

NOTE

 

• Mercury (Option 1): The smallest planet and the closest to the sun. It rotates in the ordinary direction, and has the greatest range of temperature of any planet.

 

• Neptune (Option 2): The farthest planet from the sun, and the windiest. It was discovered by mathematical prediction rather than by observation.

 

• Mars (Option 3): The "Red Planet", so coloured by iron oxide. It has the largest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, and two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

question: "Kajri", the folk song of the rainy season sung chiefly by women, belongs to which region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eastern Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kajri is the folk song of the monsoon, belonging to EASTERN UTTAR PRADESH — above all to Mirzapur, Varanasi and Banaras — and to the neighbouring parts of Bihar. (कजरी — पूर्वी उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• It is sung in the month of Sawan (July-August), chiefly by women, and its themes are the coming of the rains and the longing of a wife for a husband who is away.

 

• The name is traced to kajal (the darkness of the rain clouds), and by tradition to the goddess Kajmal of Mirzapur.

 

• The Kajri of Mirzapur is the most celebrated form, and there is a saying that Kajri belongs to Mirzapur as thumri belongs to Banaras.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Seasonal folk songs of northern India:

 

• Kajri – the rains, Sawan

 

• Chaiti – the month of Chaitra, in spring

 

• Hori and Phag – Holi

 

• Barahmasa – a song of all twelve months

 

• Sohar – sung at the birth of a child; Banna-Banni – at weddings

 

• Kajri, Chaiti, Hori and Jhula together form the semi-classical group often sung after a thumri in a Hindustani recital.

 

NOTE

 

• Malwa (Option 2): The plateau of western Madhya Pradesh, known for Nirgun bhajans and the Malwi Lok Geet.

 

• Bundelkhand (Option 3): Known for the heroic ballad Alha, sung of the deeds of Alha and Udal, and also traditionally in the rainy season — which makes it a genuine distractor.

 

• Marwar (Option 4): The desert region of western Rajasthan, known for Panihari, Maand and the music of the Manganiyars and Langas.

question: According to the Census of 2011, what was the literacy rate of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 74.04 per cent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Census of 2011, India's literacy rate was 74.04%. (साक्षरता दर 2011 — 74.04 प्रतिशत)

 

• Male literacy was 82.14% and female literacy 65.46%, a gap of nearly 17 percentage points.

 

• The highest literacy was in Kerala (93.91%), followed by Lakshadweep and Mizoram; the lowest was in Bihar (63.82%).

 

• Lakshadweep had the highest male literacy, and Kerala the highest female literacy.

 

• A person is counted as literate in the Census if he or she is aged seven or above and can both read and write with understanding in any language. The ability to read alone is not enough.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other key figures from the Census of 2011:

 

• Population – 121.09 crore

 

• Decadal growth – 17.7%

 

• Sex ratio – 943 females per 1,000 males

 

• Child sex ratio (0-6 years) – 919

 

• Density – 382 persons per sq km

 

• Urban population – 31.16%

 

• The Census of 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since independence. Its slogan was *"Our Census, Our Future"*.

 

NOTE

 

• 64.8 per cent (Option 1): The literacy rate recorded by the Census of 2001. This is the strongest distractor, and the figure most often confused with the later one.

 

• 80.9 per cent (Option 3): No census has recorded this figure. Sample surveys of later years have reported rates above 77%, but not from a census.

 

• 68.3 per cent (Option 4): Not a census figure for literacy at all.

question: The Vernacular Press Act, which imposed restrictions on newspapers published in Indian languages, was passed during the term of which Viceroy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Lytton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 under Lord Lytton, Viceroy from 1876 to 1880. (वर्नाक्युलर प्रेस एक्ट — लॉर्ड लिटन, 1878)

 

• Its purpose was to suppress criticism of the government in Indian-language newspapers, and it made no such provision for the English-language press — which is why it was called the "Gagging Act".

 

• A magistrate could require the printer of an Indian-language paper to give a bond and a deposit, both forfeit if anything objectionable were published, and there was no right of appeal to a court.

 

• The Amrita Bazar Patrika famously escaped it by converting itself overnight into an English newspaper.

 

• It was repealed in 1882 by Lord Ripon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Lytton's term is remembered for three things, all unpopular:

 

• The Vernacular Press Act, 1878

 

• The Arms Act, 1878, which forbade Indians to keep arms without a licence

 

• The Delhi Durbar of 1877, held to proclaim Queen Victoria Empress of India, at the height of a famine in which lakhs died

 

• He also lowered the maximum age for the Indian Civil Service examination from 21 to 19, making it still harder for Indians to compete.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Ripon (Option 1): Viceroy 1880-84, and the one who repealed the Act in 1882. He is remembered as the "Father of Local Self-Government" for his resolution of 1882, and for the Ilbert Bill controversy.

 

• Lord Dufferin (Option 2): Viceroy 1884-88, during whose term the Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.

 

• Lord Curzon (Option 3): Viceroy 1899-1905, who carried out the Partition of Bengal (1905) and the Indian Universities Act (1904), and who founded the Archaeological Survey of India in its modern form.

question: According to the Census of 2011, what was the overall sex ratio of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 943.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The overall sex ratio of India in the Census of 2011 was 943 females per 1,000 males. (लिंगानुपात 2011 — 943)

 

• This was an improvement on the 933 recorded in 2001, and the highest figure since 1961.

 

• The child sex ratio (0-6 years), however, fell to 919 in 2011 from 927 in 2001 — the lowest since independence. The two figures moving in opposite directions is the most discussed feature of the 2011 data.

 

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio, at 1,084, and remains the only state with more women than men. Haryana had the lowest, at 879.

 

• Among the union territories, Puducherry was highest at 1,037 and Daman & Diu lowest at 618.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sex ratio is defined in India as the number of females per 1,000 males. Note that in most other countries the ratio is expressed the other way about.

 

• The fall in the child sex ratio led to the strengthening of the PCPNDT Act, 1994, which prohibits prenatal sex determination, and to the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao scheme launched in 2015 from Panipat.

 

• The NFHS-5 (2019-21) later reported a sex ratio of 1,020 women per 1,000 men — the first survey to show women outnumbering men in India, though it is a sample survey and not a census.

 

NOTE

 

• 918 (Option 1): Close to the child sex ratio (0-6 years) of 919 recorded in 2011, and the commonest confusion in this question.

 

• 933 (Option 2): The overall sex ratio recorded in the Census of 2001 — the previous decade's figure.

 

• 972 (Option 4): Not a national figure from any recent census. Several individual states record ratios near it.

question: The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is an initiative of which Union Ministry?
option_1: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
option_4: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is an initiative of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, taken forward by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). (ओएनडीसी — वाणिज्य एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय)

 

• It was launched in 2021 and its pilot began in 2022.

 

• Its purpose is to break the hold of a few large platforms on e-commerce. Instead of buyers and sellers having to be on the same application, ONDC creates an open network on which a buyer using any compliant app can transact with a seller registered on any other.

 

• It is built on open protocols, on the model of UPI in payments, and is meant to bring small retailers and kirana shops into digital commerce on equal terms.

 

• It is incorporated as a Section 8 (not-for-profit) company.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Digital public infrastructure in India, and the ministries behind it:

 

• UPI – National Payments Corporation of India, under the RBI

 

• Aadhaar – UIDAI, under the Ministry of Electronics and IT

 

• DigiLocker, UMANG, BHASHINI – Ministry of Electronics and IT

 

• ONDC – Ministry of Commerce and Industry

 

• GeM (Government e-Marketplace) – also under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Electronics and IT (Option 1): The strongest distractor, since it is responsible for most of India's digital public infrastructure — Aadhaar, DigiLocker, UMANG and BHASHINI. ONDC, being a commerce initiative, is the exception.

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 3): Responsible for the financial regulators and for the Budget, but not for ONDC.

 

• Ministry of Consumer Affairs (Option 4): Frames the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, which regulate online sellers — a related but distinct function.

question: Why does a swimming pool filled with clear water appear shallower than it actually is?
option_1: Because light is refracted as it passes from water into air
option_2: Because light is reflected at the surface of the water
option_3: Because light is scattered by particles suspended in the water
option_4: Because of total internal reflection at the bottom of the pool
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because light is refracted as it passes from water into air.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A pool appears shallower than it is because of the REFRACTION of light — the bending of a ray as it passes from one medium into another of different optical density. (अपवर्तन — तालाब उथला दिखाई देना)

 

• Light travelling from a point at the bottom of the pool passes from water (denser) into air (rarer), and in doing so bends away from the normal.

 

• The eye, however, assumes that light has travelled in a straight line. It therefore traces the bent ray backwards along its final direction and locates the point higher than it really is.

 

• What the observer sees is the apparent depth, which is less than the real depth. The relation is:

 

• Refractive index = real depth ÷ apparent depth

 

• Since the refractive index of water is about 1.33, a pool 4 metres deep appears about 3 metres deep.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Refraction explains several other familiar effects:

 

• A stick partly in water appears bent at the surface

 

• A coin at the bottom of a bowl becomes visible when water is poured in

 

• Letters appear raised when a thick glass slab is placed on a page

 

• The twinkling of stars and the early appearance of the sun at dawn

 

NOTE

 

• Reflection at the surface (Option 2): Reflection produces the image of the sky on the water, not a change in apparent depth.

 

• Scattering by particles (Option 3): Scattering makes water look cloudy or coloured. The question specifies clear water, and in any case scattering does not shift the apparent position of the bottom.

 

• Total internal reflection (Option 4): Occurs when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium beyond the critical angle, and is reflected back entirely. It explains the mirage, the sparkle of a diamond and the working of optical fibres — but here the light does emerge from the water, so the reflection is not total.

question: The disease commonly known as "Mpox" is caused by a virus belonging to which group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Orthopoxvirus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mpox, formerly called monkeypox, is caused by a virus of the genus ORTHOPOXVIRUS, of the family Poxviridae. (एमपॉक्स — ऑर्थोपॉक्सवायरस)

 

• The same genus includes the variola virus, which causes smallpox, and the vaccinia virus, from which the smallpox vaccine was made. This relationship is why smallpox vaccination gives substantial protection against mpox.

 

• It is a zoonotic disease — one transmitted from animals to human beings — and although first identified in laboratory monkeys in 1958, its natural reservoir is believed to be rodents.

 

• Its symptoms are fever, headache, muscle ache, swollen lymph nodes and a characteristic rash that passes through several stages.

 

• The World Health Organization renamed the disease "Mpox" in 2022, to avoid the stigma and the geographical misdirection attached to the older name.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Smallpox remains the only human disease ever eradicated, declared so by the WHO in 1980. India was declared smallpox-free in 1977.

 

• Diseases and their causes — a set worth knowing:

 

• Viral – influenza, measles, polio, rabies, dengue, chikungunya, AIDS, mpox

 

• Bacterial – tuberculosis, cholera, typhoid, tetanus, plague, leprosy

 

• Protozoan – malaria, kala-azar, amoebic dysentery, sleeping sickness

 

• Fungal – ringworm, athlete's foot

 

NOTE

 

• Flavivirus (Option 1): The genus of the viruses causing dengue, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis and Zika — all spread by mosquitoes.

 

• Coronavirus (Option 3): The family responsible for COVID-19, SARS and MERS, named for the crown-like spikes seen under the microscope.

 

• Retrovirus (Option 4): The group to which HIV belongs. A retrovirus carries its genetic material as RNA and converts it into DNA inside the host cell, using the enzyme reverse transcriptase.

question: India became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2017.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in 2017, at the Astana summit held in Kazakhstan. Pakistan was admitted at the same time. (एससीओ — भारत 2017 में पूर्ण सदस्य)

 

• India had been an observer since 2005, and applied for full membership in 2014.

 

• The SCO was founded in 2001 at Shanghai by six countries — China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan — which had earlier formed the "Shanghai Five".

 

• Iran joined as a full member in 2023 and Belarus in 2024.

 

• Its headquarters — the Secretariat — is at Beijing, and its counter-terrorism arm, the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS), is at Tashkent.

 

• India hosted the SCO summit in 2023, in virtual format.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SCO's stated purposes are security cooperation, counter-terrorism, and economic and cultural exchange among its members.

 

• India's membership of other groupings:

 

• BRICS – founding member as BRIC in 2009; South Africa added 2010

 

• G20 – founding member, 1999; hosted the summit in 2023

 

• QUAD – with the United States, Japan and Australia

 

• BIMSTEC, IORA, Commonwealth, NAM — and India is not a member of OPEC, NATO or the G7.

 

NOTE

 

• 2005 (Option 1): The year India was granted observer status — a genuine milestone, and the strongest distractor here.

 

• 2012 (Option 2): No change in India's SCO status occurred in this year.

 

• 2020 (Option 3): The year India hosted the SCO Heads of Government meeting, three years after becoming a member.

question: The first modern Olympic Games, held in 1896, took place in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Athens.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first modern Olympic Games were held at ATHENS, Greece, in 1896. (प्रथम आधुनिक ओलंपिक — एथेंस, 1896)

 

• Athens was chosen because the ancient Olympic Games had been held in Greece, at Olympia, from 776 BCE until they were abolished in 393 CE.

 

• The revival was the work of Baron Pierre de Coubertin, a French educationist, who founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894. He is called the father of the modern Olympics.

 

• The 1896 Games had 241 athletes from 14 countries, competing in 43 events. No women took part; women first competed at Paris in 1900.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Olympic motto was "Citius, Altius, Fortius" — Faster, Higher, Stronger — to which "Communiter" ("Together") was added in 2021.

 

• The five rings represent the five inhabited continents, and the six colours — blue, yellow, black, green, red and the white background — were chosen because every national flag then contained at least one of them.

 

• The IOC headquarters is at Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• India first participated in 1900, when Norman Pritchard won two silver medals in athletics.

 

NOTE

 

• Paris (Option 1): Host of the second modern Games in 1900, and again in 1924 and 2024 — making it, with London, one of the two cities to have hosted three times.

 

• London (Option 3): Host in 1908, 1948 and 2012.

 

• Rome (Option 4): Host in 1960, at which Milkha Singh finished fourth in the 400 metres by a hundredth of a second.

question: "Unbreakable" is the autobiography of which Indian sportsperson?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mary Kom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Unbreakable" is the autobiography of the boxer Mary Kom (Mangte Chungneijang Mary Kom), published in 2013. (अनब्रेकेबल — मैरी कॉम)

 

• She is the only woman to have won six World Amateur Boxing Championships, and the only woman boxer to have won a medal in each of the first seven world championships.

 

• She won a bronze medal at the London Olympics of 2012, the first Indian woman boxer to win an Olympic medal.

 

• She is from Manipur, and is known as "Magnificent Mary".

 

• She received the Padma Shri (2006), the Padma Bhushan (2013), the Padma Vibhushan (2020) and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2009), and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 2016.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Autobiographies and biographies of Indian sportspersons:

 

• "Unbreakable" – Mary Kom

 

• "The Race of My Life" – Milkha Singh

 

• "Playing It My Way" – Sachin Tendulkar

question:
Which of the following statements regarding the economic reforms of 1991 is/are correct?

I. Disinvestment means the sale of a part of the equity holding of the government in a public sector undertaking.
II. Under the New Industrial Policy of 1991, industrial licensing was abolished for every industry without exception.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is CORRECT. Disinvestment is the sale of a part of the government's equity holding in a public sector undertaking. (विनिवेश)

 

• Where the government sells enough to give up management control, the step is called strategic disinvestment or privatisation — as with Air India, sold to the Tata group in 2022.

 

• Statement II is INCORRECT. Industrial licensing was abolished for most industries in 1991, but not for all. A short list was kept, and licensing remains for a handful of industries on grounds of security, health and the environment.

 

• Those still requiring a licence include alcoholic drinks, tobacco products, defence equipment, industrial explosives and certain hazardous chemicals.

 

• The number of industries reserved for the public sector was likewise reduced from 17 to 8 in 1991, and stands at two today — atomic energy and railway operations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The New Economic Policy of 1991 is summarised as LPG — Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation, and was introduced by Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao with Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.

 

• Its other measures: the devaluation of the rupee in July 1991, the abolition of the MRTP asset limits, the reduction of import tariffs, and the opening of many sectors to foreign direct investment.

 

NOTE

 

• Since Statement I is correct and Statement II is not, Option 2 (Only II), Option 3 (Both I and II) and Option 4 (Neither I nor II) are all ruled out.

 

• Statement II is a good example of a claim made false by a single overreaching word. Licensing was indeed abolished for most industries; the words "without exception" are what make the statement wrong.

question: How many players are there in each team on the court in a game of Kabaddi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A team in Kabaddi has SEVEN players on the court, with five more held in reserve, making a squad of twelve. (कबड्डी — प्रत्येक टीम में 7 खिलाड़ी)

 

• A match consists of two halves of 20 minutes each, with a five-minute interval.

 

• A player of the attacking side, the raider, enters the opponents' half chanting "kabaddi" in a single breath, attempts to touch one or more defenders, and must return to his own half before the breath is exhausted.

 

• When all seven players of a side are put out, the opposing team scores a "lona" — a bonus of two points.

 

• Kabaddi is the state game of several Indian states, and India has won the Kabaddi gold at every Asian Games at which it has been played since 1990, with two exceptions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Number of players per side — a set that is examined constantly:

 

• Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Polo (elephant/water), Handball (7 including goalkeeper) – 7

 

• Volleyball, Handball on court excluding goalkeeper, Water Polo, Baseball – 6 or 9 (baseball 9)

 

• Basketball, Netball – 5 and 7

 

• Hockey, Football – 11; Cricket – 11

 

• Rugby – 15; Ice hockey – 6; Badminton doubles / Tennis doubles – 2

 

NOTE

 

• 5 (Option 1): The number in basketball, and also the number of reserve players in a kabaddi squad — which makes it a genuine distractor.

 

• 9 (Option 3): The number in baseball and in softball.

 

• 11 (Option 4): The number in cricket, hockey and football.

question: The Banaras Hindu University was founded by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madan Mohan Malaviya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Banaras Hindu University (BHU) was founded by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1916, under the Banaras Hindu University Act, 1915. (काशी हिंदू विश्वविद्यालय — मदन मोहन मालवीय)

 

• It is one of the largest residential universities in Asia, with a campus of about 1,300 acres at Varanasi.

 

• Malaviya raised the funds for it by public subscription, travelling across India for the purpose, and is remembered as "Mahamana".

 

• He was four times President of the Indian National Congress, founded the newspaper "The Leader", and was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2015.

 

• The slogan "Satyameva Jayate" was popularised by him, and it was adopted as the national motto.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Institutions and their founders — a set worth memorising:

 

• Banaras Hindu University (1916) – Madan Mohan Malaviya

 

• Aligarh Muslim University, from the MAO College (1875) – Syed Ahmad Khan

 

• Santiniketan (1901) and Visva-Bharati (1921) – Rabindranath Tagore

 

• Servants of India Society (1905) – Gopal Krishna Gokhale

 

• Jamia Millia Islamia (1920) – Maulana Mehmud Hasan and Dr. Zakir Husain

 

• Gujarat Vidyapith (1920) – Mahatma Gandhi

 

NOTE

 

• Annie Besant (Option 1): The strongest distractor, and for good reason. She founded the Central Hindu College at Banaras in 1898, and that college became the nucleus of BHU when the university was established. But the university itself was Malaviya's creation. She was also the first woman President of the Congress, in 1917, and founder of the Home Rule League.

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 2): Founder of the Servants of India Society (1905) and Gandhi's political mentor.

 

• Syed Ahmad Khan (Option 3): Founder of the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875, which became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920, and leader of the Aligarh Movement.

question: Which freedom fighter is remembered by the title "Frontier Gandhi"?

solution_text:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan is remembered as the "Frontier Gandhi" — and among his own people as Badshah Khan or Bacha Khan. (सीमांत गांधी — खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान)

 

• He led the freedom struggle in the North-West Frontier Province, and founded the Khudai Khidmatgars ("Servants of God") in 1929, a non-violent volunteer force whose members wore red shirts — from which they were called the Red Shirts (Surkh Posh).

 

• That a movement of strict non-violence should have taken root among the Pathans, a people of famously martial tradition, is what made his achievement remarkable, and what earned him the comparison with Gandhi.

 

• He opposed the Partition of India, and said of the Congress decision to accept it that the Pathans had been *"thrown to the wolves"*.

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1987 — the first non-Indian to receive it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Titles and epithets of national leaders — a set frequently examined:

 

• Shaheed-e-Azam – Bhagat Singh; Punjab Kesari – Lala Lajpat Rai

 

• Lokmanya – Bal Gangadhar Tilak; Deshbandhu – Chittaranjan Das

 

• Netaji – Subhas Chandra Bose; Sardar – Vallabhbhai Patel

 

• Rajaji – C. Rajagopalachari; Mahamana – Madan Mohan Malaviya

 

• Gurudev – Rabindranath Tagore; Loknayak – Jayaprakash Narayan

 

• Frontier Gandhi – Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan

 

NOTE

 

• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (Option 1): The youngest President of the Congress at 35, and independent India's first Education Minister. His birthday, 11 November, is observed as National Education Day, and he wrote "India Wins Freedom".

 

• Dr. Zakir Husain (Option 3): The third President of India and its first Muslim President, and a founder of Jamia Millia Islamia.

 

• Hakim Ajmal Khan (Option 4): A physician of Unani medicine and a nationalist leader, the only person to have presided over the Congress, the Muslim League and the Khilafat Conference.
